topic.title: Generating Scalar
topic.shortdesc: Changing how an interactive API reference looks and behaves by editing scalar.json in the data store.

section.title: How API References Are Rendered
section.p: A topic generated from an OpenAPI file contains a single ScalarApiReference node. The renderer turns that node into an interactive Scalar API reference. The node carries only the location of the spec:
specUrl is relative to the topic's own directory in the data store. Settings are not stored in the topic; every API reference on the site reads the same scalar.json.

section.title: Editing the Settings
section.p: Edit scalar.json in the root of the data store directory (next to chrome.json). It is a flat JSON object of Scalar configuration options:

The data store serves the file as a static asset at /data/scalar.json and the browser reads it each time an API reference loads. Reload the page to see a change; there is no rebuild. If the file is missing, the renderer falls back to hideClientButton: true and withDefaultFonts: false.
section.note: There is no transtype or REST endpoint for scalar.json. If you refresh the data store with rsync --delete, the file is removed unless it is part of the source directory or excluded with --exclude=scalar.json.

plentry.pd: modern (two columns, operations expanded) or classic (operations as collapsed cards).
Show or hide Scalar's own sidebar and search. The harness already provides a table of contents, so both are normally off. The sidebar cannot start collapsed; it is either shown or hidden.
Control which tag groups start expanded.
Language targets to remove from the Client Libraries list. Entries may be a target such as node, a client such as fetch, or a full id such as node/fetch.
both, yaml, json, direct or none.

section.title: Settings the Renderer Controls
section.p: A few settings are applied by the renderer after scalar.json is read, so values in the file have no effect:

ul.li: url — always resolved from the node's specUrl.
forceDarkModeState — follows the harness light/dark switch. Scalar's own toggle is not shown, and the API reference reloads when the theme changes.

localization.locale — taken from the topic language, so a German topic renders Scalar in German. Scalar includes English, Russian, Spanish, French, German, Chinese (Simplified), Arabic and Portuguese.
